To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the carbon coating of LMS and the carbon coating of LCS were obtained by using the same precursor, (2) the carbon coating process of LCS leads to the decomposition of the active material and (3) the carbon coating on LMS is possible with the reconstruction of the crystalline structure of the active material.
the formation of CCLs on LMS grains in the Li/Li+/LMS composites can be successfully performed using PMA modified PNVF as a carbon precursor.
the stability of Li2MSO4 (Mn, Co), in the CCL/Li2MSiO (M = Mn, Co) compositing process, can be enhanced by using PMA modified PNVF carbon precursors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a simple and effective approach for the synthesis of carbon coated Li2MSiOs (M = Mn, Co).
the stability of Li2MSO4 (Mn, Co)-based cathode materials in the carbon coating synthesis process.
the stability of Li2MSio4 (M =Mn, Co)/carbon composites under reductive and oxidative conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCL/LMS composites are stable in oxidizing atmosphere while the CCL/LCS composites are stable under reductive atmosphere.
the stability of the carbon layer is higher on the LMS grains than on LCS.
the carbon coating on the LMS grains can be performed by using the standard pyrolytic process while it is impossible for LCS grains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of Li2MSO4 (Mn, Co), in the carbon coating forming process, can be improved by the addition of carbon precursor with a strong acid group.
carbon coating of Li2MSO4 (Mn, Co)-based cathodes can be performed by using PMA modified PNFV precursor.
the carbon coatings on the LMS grains are more stable under oxidizing conditions and the LMS/CCL composites can be more suitable for the Li-ion battery applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain the stable CCL/LMS composites, but not CCL/LCS composites.
the CCL/LCS nanocomposites are not suitable for lithium-ion battery anodes.

the carbon coating can be formed on the surface of LMS grains without the loss of the crystalline structure, and it is possible to improve the surface stability of the LMS and LCS by the carbon coating process.
